record.original_question: How does the supernova phenomenon evolve with metallicity, stellar population, cosmic age, environment, and other relevant parameters across cosmic time, and how should those dependencies be included when using supernovae to understand how the universe works and evolves?

evidence.quote: While studying any type of SN and any aspect of their explosions, one should also consider the cosmic evolution of the SN phenomenon as a function of important parameters such as (i) metallicity, (ii) stellar population, (iii) cosmic age, and (iv) environment.
The point is that we are not studying SNe just to understand SNe, but rather because we want to understand how the Universe works and evolve.

artifact.status_search_result: The cosmic evolution of supernova populations with metallicity, progenitor stellar population, redshift, and environment remains an active and unresolved area of research in astrophysics. While significant progress has been made (e.g., observed metallicity trends in stripped-envelope SNe, host-galaxy mass step in Type Ia cosmology, evolving SN rates with redshift), a complete quantitative characterization and a fully validated framework for incorporating these dependencies into precision cosmology has not been achieved.

status_evidence.title: Type Ia Supernova Cosmology systematics review
status_evidence.snippet: Host-galaxy correlations and potential progenitor evolution remain leading systematic uncertainties in SN Ia cosmology.
status_evidence.claim: Dependencies of SN observables on host environment and cosmic epoch are still being characterized and corrected for.
